title: Ergotropy of multipartite entangled states in the quantum atmosphere
abstract: We investigate the ergotropy of tripartite Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger (GHZ) and W states in the quantum atmosphere of a Schwarzschild black hole, focusing on how the extractable work is redistributed under Hawking-induced thermalization. We find that the two classes of multipartite entanglement exhibit qualitatively different ergotropy structures. For GHZ states, the ergotropies associated with different accessible subsystems organize into two degenerate families, whereas for W states they obey a linear averaging relation with no counterpart in the GHZ case. Under symmetric gravitational thermal corrections, the two GHZ families remain separated by a constant energy gap that is independent of the radial position. We further show that the Hartle-Hawking constant $D_{HH}$ and the normalized radial distance $r/r_h$ play competing roles in the evolution of extractable work: increasing $D_{HH}$ suppresses its recovery toward the asymptotic Hawking limit, while increasing $r/r_h$ enhances the ergotropy accessible to the observers. These results show that the redistribution of extractable work in a black-hole environment is governed not only by gravitationally induced thermalization but also by the structure of the underlying multipartite entanglement, providing a thermodynamic signature that distinguishes GHZ- and W-type quantum correlations in curved spacetime.
summary: This work studies the extractable work (ergotropy) of entangled quantum states (GHZ and W) near a black hole horizon. It finds that the way this work is lost or recovered depends critically on the initial entanglement structure and the local gravitational environment. The results establish a thermodynamic signature distinguishing different types of quantum correlations in curved spacetime.
main_problem: The paper investigates how the extractable work (ergotropy) of multipartite entangled states is redistributed in the quantum atmosphere of a Schwarzschild black hole due to Hawking-induced thermalization.
main_result: The ergotropy structures for GHZ and W states are qualitatively different, and the work recovery is governed by a competition between the Hartle-Hawking constant and the radial distance.
method: The analysis uses quantum thermodynamics applied to curved spacetime, calculating ergotropy based on the energy spectrum of reduced density matrices derived from the Dirac field quantization.
model_or_system: The system models tripartite GHZ and W entangled states evolving in the quantum atmosphere near a Schwarzschild black hole, incorporating gravitational thermal corrections.
key_observables: Ergotropy ($E(ho)$), which quantifies the maximum extractable work.
important_parameters: Hartle-Hawking constant ($D_{HH}$), normalized radial distance ($r/r_h$), and the structure of the initial entanglement (GHZ vs. W).
main_assumptions: The analysis is performed in the Hartle-Hawking vacuum, and the reduced states are constructed by tracing out complementary modes near the horizon.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the evolution of ergotropy for both GHZ and W states as a function of radial position, showing characteristic peaks, dips, and recovery trends.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by introducing the problem and defining ergotropy, reviewing the curved spacetime quantization, and then analyzing the specific mathematical forms and radial dependencies of the ergotropy for GHZ and W states.
why_interesting: It provides a concrete example of how fundamental quantum resources (entanglement) interact with gravitational thermodynamics, offering a measurable, non-equilibrium signature in curved spacetime.
